deviations: Grant script src/sql/grants/MOD-013.sql uses the placeholder role [<analyst_role>] (as MOD-001 does): the name of the analyst role that runs the usp_report_* procedures is not known. A human replaces it and runs the script.

A paid position whose Campaign Year has no Layercake.ref_campaign_year_config row is still counted in its year, but its derived date cannot be compared with a year end, so it does not count. The design does not cover this case. It should not happen, because every Phase 1 silver run adds any missing Campaign Year (answers.md, MOD-007 carry-forward and campaign-year config).
notes:
Layercake.usp_report_retirement_comparison @as_of_date date = NULL (accepted and ignored, ADR-003). It returns one row per Campaign Year that has a silv_payment_events row, ordered by campaign_year, with the seven columns from ASM-004. Before the build, all 11 test_MOD013 tests failed because the procedure did not exist. Now all 11 test_MOD013 tests and all 5 test_MOD013_dev tests pass.

How the report decides each group:
- Retired concession: the year's silv_member_year_attributes.concession_type_id joined to silv_ref_concession_type.item_code, which must be one of the six retired codes. The match uses the database collation, so it ignores case. A paid position with no attributes row has no retired concession.
- Derived date: read from Layercake.vw_silv_derived_retirement_date (MOD-018), the same definition usp_load_silv_member_base uses. It counts only when it is on or before that year's campaign_year_end, in every group (ASM-005).
- apuk_retirementdate and silv_member_base are not read.
- Agreement rate: ROUND(100 * (retired_concession_and_date + neither) / paid_positions, 1), returned as decimal(5,1).
- Every join is on a unique key, so no position is counted twice.

The dev unit tests cover: a paid position with no attributes row; a year with no config row; a case-variant retired item code; attributes rows with no paid position, which produce no rows; and rounding (16.7, 83.3).

Grant: EXECUTE for [<analyst_role>]; a human runs the script.

Test-first: the first run had 0 of 11 of the Tester's tests passing; the final run passed 11 of 11 and 5 unit test(s), in 4 run(s).
